definition: The legal standard established in United States v. Bajakajian for determining when a fine is excessive under the Eighth Amendment. A fine violates the Excessive Fines Clause if it is 'grossly disproportionate' to the gravity of the offense — meaning the punishment is wildly out of step with how serious the wrongdoing actually was.
examples: The central dispute in this case is how courts should apply the gross disproportionality test — Jouppi says the Alaska Supreme Court applied it too leniently.
